quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: What color is a warning sign with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Is the front brake safe?

options.text: Only to be used if the rear brake fails.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safe, if used properly.
questions.explanation: The front brake is safe when used correctly. It is stronger than the rear brake and provides most of the stopping power.

questions.question: Is riding at night easier or harder than riding during the day?

options.text: Easier because you can see other vehicle lights better.
Harder because it is more difficult to see.
Less distracting than riding during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder because it is more difficult to see.
questions.explanation: Night riding is harder because you cannot see as well. It is also harder to judge distances without normal shadows and light.

questions.question: What type of clothing helps other drivers see you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Reflective clothes
questions.explanation: Wear bright, reflective clothing. It makes it easier for other drivers to spot you.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
Others may be driving slowly looking for a spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
questions.explanation: A driver may pull out of a parking space without looking. Car doors may open into your lane. Pedestrians may step out from between cars.

questions.question: Why should you maintain a safe following distance?

options.text: To give you time and space to see and react to hazards.
To help traffic counters count you as a vehicle.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give you time and space to see and react to hazards.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance gives you space to stop or swerve if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. You also get a better view of the road, such as potholes.

questions.question: If you wait one hour per drink before riding, are you safe to ride?

options.text: Yes, you cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Yes, your skills will not be affected.
No, side effects may still remain.
Yes, as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, side effects may still remain.
questions.explanation: Your body can eliminate about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your system and affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: How many brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.correctAnswerText: Front and rear
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.

questions.question: What brakes do most motorcycles have?

options.text: Brakes in both the front and rear.
Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes in both the front and rear.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: Which of these is not important when choosing a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: The helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
The helmet fits snugly all the way around your head.
The helmet has no visible defects, such as cracks or loose padding.

questions.correctAnswerText: The helmet looks cool.
questions.explanation: Check that your helmet meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly all around your head, and has no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. How it looks is not important for safety.

questions.question: What should you NOT check before getting on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Paint damage.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check tire tread and air pressure, oil and fluid levels, lights, and signals.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than on a car. Always inspect your motorcycle before every ride.

questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane while following a car, what happens?

options.text: You are in the best position to be seen.
The driver may not see you unless they use their side mirror.
The driver will know you are there.
You stop other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not see you unless they use their side mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver sees you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors.

questions.question: What should you do before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle?

options.text: Ride it like your own bike, since all bikes are the same.
Check the controls and shift pattern.
Trust the owner that everything works.
Assume you know where the controls are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the controls and shift pattern.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Check the controls and gear pattern before riding. Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times first.

questions.question: When should you wear a jacket on a motorcycle?

options.text: Only for rides longer than 30 minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter the weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding. Even in hot weather, it protects you from the sun and helps prevent dehydration.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol quickly?

options.text: More alcohol builds up in your body.
You are less likely to get pulled over.

questions.correctAnswerText: More alcohol builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: When you drink quickly, alcohol builds up in your body. Never ride a motorcycle after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: How noticeable is a motorcycle's brake light compared to a car's?
questions.correctAnswerText: Less noticeable.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle brake light is usually less noticeable than a car's brake lights. Flash your brake light before slowing or stopping to help other drivers see you.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a motorcycle crash?

options.text: Wear a quality helmet that is fastened securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a quality helmet that is fastened securely.
questions.explanation: Wearing a quality helmet that is fastened securely is the single most effective way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: What is important to remember about blind spots when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Motorcycles are too small to have blind spots.
Blind spots are too small to be a problem.
You need to turn your head to check them.
Motorcycles have only one blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: You need to turn your head to check them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: How should a helmet fit to give you the best protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Snugly.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly all around with no visible damage.
